ai.description: The Malabar Tree Toad (Bufonidae) reaches 5–6 cm. It is olive-brown with dark, warty skin and a distinct pale mid-dorsal stripe. It features prominent parotoid glands and large, adhesive toe discs.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Malabar Tree Toad is best distinguished by its distinct, bright yellow or orange webbing between the toes, which is absent in other similar-looking Indian tree toads.
ai.habitat: The Malabar Tree Toad inhabits evergreen and semi-evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found near streams at elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Malabar Tree Toad is primarily nocturnal and utilizes its specialized toe pads to remain camouflaged against tree bark during the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Malabar Tree Toad breeds in tree hollows during the monsoon season (June–August), laying small clutches of eggs that develop into tadpoles within the water-filled cavities.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Malabar Tree Toad is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, found in states like Kerala, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 200 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Malabar Tree Toad emits a high-pitched, rhythmic series of "tink-tink-tink" notes, typically heard from vegetation near streams during the monsoon season.
